# Cedarwood Studio

> A one-person software and infrastructure studio. Two fixed-price services: a Rails Upgrade Roadmap built from a sandbox run of the upgrade ($2,500), and a CI Diagnostic for GitHub Actions ($500). The measured pages below come from public sample repositories that can be checked line by line.

Cedarwood Studio is the business name of Jack Senechal, a sole proprietor. Contact: hello@cedarwood.studio. Prices are in US dollars and are fixed. Each page below carries the date it was last updated.

## Services

- [Rails Upgrade Roadmap, $2,500 fixed](https://cedarwood.studio/rails-upgrade-roadmap/): A checked test run of a Rails application's upgrade in a sandbox: the dependency resolver at every version step, the test suite, a start-up check under each configuration, a trial of the first version step, a read of the code the tests never run, and a separate review pass. The deliverable is a report of what broke plus a staged plan. Credited toward an upgrade started with the studio; the upgrade itself is quoted separately. Rails only, for upgrades that start at 7.0 or later and end at 8.1 or earlier, with test suites that need no service beyond MariaDB and Redis; earlier Rails versions and PostgreSQL test databases are not offered yet. Last updated 2026-11-17.
- [CI Diagnostic, $500 fixed](https://cedarwood.studio/github-actions-ci-diagnostic/): A written report on a slow or flaky GitHub Actions pipeline, measured from its run history: run time and where it goes, failure and re-run rates, jobs that failed and then passed on the same commit, unpinned or deprecated actions, dependency cache hit rates, and changes ranked by what they save. GitHub Actions only. Failing tests are named for pytest and unittest; other test runners get run-level numbers. CircleCI is not offered. Last updated 2026-11-17.

## Measured answers

- [What breaks when upgrading Rails 7.1 to 8, and how long does each stage take?](https://cedarwood.studio/rails-7-1-to-8-upgrade-what-broke/): One measured upgrade of an open-source Rails application (Postal, about 27,000 lines, 851 test examples) from Rails 7.1.6 to 8.0.5.2: the eight lines flagged as breaking on the path to 8.1, how each was found, and the machine time for each stage and review (81 minutes building, 109 minutes of review, no human time measured). Last updated 2026-11-17.
- [Can an AI agent do a Rails upgrade?](https://cedarwood.studio/can-an-ai-agent-do-a-rails-upgrade/): A first-hand account with figures. The first automated pass on an open-source Rails application (Rails 7.1 toward 8.1, about 27,000 lines) took 16.1 minutes, found 4 of 8 breaking lines and shipped a stage that passed every check and failed to start with an optional feature on. An independent review step, wider rules and baselines generated from the runs were added; the second run found all eight, with the caution that four were found by rules written after the review named them. Last updated 2026-11-17.

## Public samples

- [cedarwood-studio/upgrade-roadmap-sample](https://github.com/cedarwood-studio/upgrade-roadmap-sample): one complete Upgrade Roadmap for Postal, an open-source Rails application (Rails 7.1 to 8.1), the record of the first four stages carried out on a fork, and a script that checks the report against its data. An unsolicited sample: nobody at the Postal project asked for it, and the studio is not affiliated with the project.
- [cedarwood-studio/ci-diagnostic-sample](https://github.com/cedarwood-studio/ci-diagnostic-sample): two complete CI Diagnostic reports on open-source projects (wagtail/wagtail and temporalio/sdk-python), with the tool and the data behind every number. Unsolicited samples, not affiliated with either project.
